passage: The evening bus from the plains had already gone when Anirban closed the shutter of the tea stall in the hill town, and Dolma was waiting on the bench outside. A month ago Anirban had found the messages. Dolma had lied within their marriage, and there was nothing to argue about. Tonight there were questions. Where, how long, who else knew. Dolma answered each one plainly, even when the answer was ugly, without adding "but". When Anirban's voice cracked with anger, Dolma stayed on the bench and did not look away. At the end Dolma said, "I'm not asking you to forgive me quickly. I'll answer anything, any time." Anirban walked up the lane ahead, then slowed once to let Dolma catch up, and did not say anything.

qa.q: Where was Dolma waiting when Anirban closed the stall?
qa.a: On the bench outside the tea stall.

qa.q: What does Dolma want, and how can you tell?
qa.a: Dolma seems remorseful and wants the marriage to survive: Dolma stays, answers every question plainly and says, "I'm not asking you to forgive me quickly."

qa.q: Why did Dolma avoid adding "but" to the answers?
qa.a: Adding "but" would have turned honest answers into excuses and defence. Answering plainly lets Anirban see the whole truth and set the pace of trust.

qa.q: How might Anirban see Dolma's behaviour tonight?
qa.a: Anirban may feel angry and hurt but also notice the honesty, since Anirban slowed once to let Dolma catch up, though the silence shows nothing is settled.

grounding: Shows a partner who broke trust and wants the marriage to survive, accepting anger, answering questions honestly without defensiveness and letting trust return at the other's pace.
